facts.fact: On 28 September 2026 the digital economy minister cited the validation of the PSEN on RTNC; the validation date is not given in this document.
The minister listed the validation of the PSEN among the ministry's achievements, reported on 28 September 2026.
UNESCO reports that public actors, partners and experts validated the PSEN in Kinshasa on 4 August 2026, as the end of a process led by the Ministry of Digital Economy.
UNESCO says the PSEN and the SNIA set the country's orientations until 2030.
The PSEN was validated at a Kinshasa ceremony on 4 August 2026, per UNESCO.
At the 4 August 2026 ceremony in Kinshasa the minister presented the PSEN for government validation, with presentation to the Council of Ministers for adoption announced for the coming days.
The PSEN is presented as guiding digital development to the 2030 horizon.
The minister said action plans still had to be finalised, and called on ministries to turn the PSEN into programmes with indicators and budget allocations.
The minister said a monitoring and evaluation mechanism and an interministerial steering mechanism were still to be set up after validation.
The PSEN passed government validation on 4 August 2026, with adoption by the Council of Ministers to follow.
Participants at a two-day workshop on 21-22 July 2026 in Kinshasa technically validated the draft PSEN 2026-2030, subject to integrating their observations.
The policy is titled PSEN 2026-2030.
Participants recommended that the final version finalise the costing of interventions, their multi-year breakdown and the link to the MTEF and programme budget.
Experts technically validated the draft PSEN on 22 July 2026, with UNDP support.

The Plan National du Numérique says the government defined a sector policy document (Document de Politique Sectorielle, DPS) for telecommunications and ICT in 2009, referenced in its bibliography as dated July 2009.

The Plan National du Numérique says the DPS lapsed on expiry of its five-year period without the review being carried out; the end year 2014 is five years from the 2009 adoption, the document giving no year.

facts.fact: COPIREP states that the telecommunications sector policy document was approved by the Government; the page gives no approval date, so the date is the document's published year, 2009.

On 23 October 2009 the minister of Posts, Telephones and Telecommunications presented the sector policy document at a workshop that the World Bank director described as finalising the strategy; the article says the sector is about to have the document.

facts.fact: A technical validation workshop in Kinshasa on 21-22 July 2026 validated the draft Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique (PSEN) 2026-2030, subject to amendments, ahead of final adoption.
The draft PSEN covers 2026-2030, led by the Ministry of Digital Economy with UNDP technical and financial support.

At a national workshop on 21-22 July 2026 organised by the Ministry of Digital Economy with World Bank support, participants validated, subject to some amendments, the Sector Policy of the Digital Economy 2026-2030 (PSEN), as the Federation of Enterprises of Congo reports.
The Sector Policy of the Digital Economy is for 2026-2030, per the Federation of Enterprises of Congo.

facts.fact: The minister of the digital economy says the Sectoral Policy of the Digital Economy (PSEN) was presented and validated by the government on 4 August 2026, with adoption by the Council of Ministers announced as the next step.
The minister says the PSEN sets the guidelines for digital development in the DRC to the 2030 horizon.
